metrics.label: Supplier concentration (HHI), {measure}
metrics.explanation: HHI {value}: more concentrated than {pct} of comparable markets in this tool. A description of the market, not a measure of leverage.

metrics.label: Largest supplier outside the coalition, {measure}
metrics.explanation: {subject}, outside the 57-economy coalition, holds {value} of {measure} ({year}). Outside the coalition is not the same as adversarial.

metrics.label: Coalition share of {measure}
metrics.explanation: Coalition core members and partners together hold {value} of {measure} ({year}).

metrics.label: {country} net trade in the HS6 basket
metrics.explanation: Net trade of {value} in {year}: imports are {ratio} exports. Trade balance, not a share of domestic consumption.

metrics.label: {country} export feasibility (related capabilities)
metrics.explanation: Harvard Atlas feasibility {value}: how close {country}'s existing exports are to this basket. Rank {rank} of {n}.

metrics.label: {country} export growth, 2020-2024
metrics.explanation: {country} exports changed by {value} between 2020 and 2024 (nominal USD).

metrics.label: {country} annual clean-manufacturing investment
metrics.explanation: {value} invested in {year} (Clean Investment Monitor), rank {rank} of {n}.

metrics.label: {country} investment growth, 2018-2025
metrics.explanation: Investment grew {value} a year between {first} and {last}.

metrics.label: Technology readiness level (global)
metrics.explanation: Average TRL {value} across the stage's technologies (IEA Clean Energy Technology Guide). A global figure: it says how mature the technology is, not whether {country} leads.

metrics.label: Change in readiness, 2020-2025 (global)
metrics.explanation: Readiness rose {value} TRL points since 2020. Movement, not leadership.

metrics.label: Addressable market (OSI component)
metrics.explanation: Normalised OSI component, {value} on 0-1 (higher means a larger addressable market): rank {rank} of {n} economies. Compare ranks, not levels.

metrics.label: Input-cost competitiveness (OSI component)
metrics.explanation: Normalised OSI component, {value} on 0-1 (higher favours opportunity, as in the Economic Opportunity pillar): rank {rank} of {n} economies on labour, capital and energy input costs.

exports.label: world exports of the HS6 basket

components.label: Battery-management firmware, energy-management software and remote updates
components.description: Firmware and software that decide how a storage system charges, discharges and protects itself, and the pathway by which they are updated.
components.criticalFunction: Dispatch and safety of grid-connected storage
components.notes: The paper places critical BMS controls in the small yard. A BMS is often integrated with proprietary cell hardware, so replacing it may require redesign and recertification ('partial' separability). 'High' assumes fleet-scale grid services; a single behind-the-meter site would be lower. Trade data record BMS hardware, not firmware.
components.source: NEIS, Three Yards for Three Different Problems (discussion draft, Oct 2026), section 1 and Appendix A4; Benich, Stewart and Krejsa, Electrotech Moneyball (CMU CMIST, 2026)

components.label: Communications gateway and cloud fleet management
components.description: Network gateways, telemetry and the vendor's cloud services that monitor and command a storage fleet.
components.criticalFunction: Dispatch and safety of grid-connected storage
components.notes: Gateways and cloud services can usually be replaced, or segmented behind trusted equivalents, without touching the cells. Verify for each architecture.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1; Electrotech Moneyball (2026)

components.label: Battery cells (LFP and NMC)
components.description: Lithium-ion cells, the core of storage systems and electric vehicles.
components.notes: Production builds yield, process and materials-integration knowledge that bears on successor chemistries such as solid-state and sodium-ion (paper section 2). 'Moderate' consequence: losing imports would slow deployment, not disable a critical function within a year.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 2 and Appendix A4

components.label: Cathode active materials and precursors
components.description: Processed nickel- and iron-based cathode materials and their precursors.
components.notes: Cathode chemistries are qualified cell by cell; qualification times vary widely by chemistry and customer.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4 ('battery cells and materials')

components.label: Anode materials (natural and synthetic graphite)
components.description: Spherical and synthetic graphite processed into battery anode material.
components.notes: China introduced export licensing for graphite in December 2023. Treated here as non-acute for stationary storage; for defence uses the consequence would be higher and the answer could move toward the small yard.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4; public reporting on China's graphite export controls (Dec 2023)

components.label: Power conversion hardware (inverters and converters)
components.description: Power electronics that convert between DC storage or generation and the AC grid. Its firmware is assessed separately, as a control layer.
components.criticalFunction: Grid interconnection of storage and renewables
components.notes: The paper places 'selected power electronics' in the medium yard. The HS heading for static converters (8504.40) covers every end use, so trade figures are attributed to several technologies.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4

components.label: Enclosures, racking, thermal management and balance of system
components.description: Containers, racks, HVAC and other passive balance-of-system parts.
components.notes: Proxy evidence: trade in generic steel and aluminium structures (HS 7308.90 and 7610.90); no HS6 code isolates battery enclosures.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 3

components.label: Utility-scale inverter firmware and remote-access functions
components.description: The software and remote-access paths in inverters that connect solar, wind and storage to the bulk power system.
components.notes: Public documents do not yet establish how separable control functions are from proprietary inverter hardware (paper section 1), so separability is left Unknown. The August 2026 bulk-power order reaches software, firmware and remote access.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1 and Appendix A4; Executive Order 14421 (Aug 26 2026), as cited in the paper

components.label: Grid-control software (SCADA, EMS, DERMS)
components.description: Supervisory control, energy-management and distributed-resource management systems that operate the grid.
components.notes: Control software is procured as a distinct layer and can be sourced from vetted vendors. Trade data cover the hardware only (HS 9032.89), where the United States is the largest exporter.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4

components.label: Large power transformers
components.description: High-voltage transformers that step power up and down across the transmission system.
components.notes: Critical and scarce, but supplied mainly by coalition members: a capacity problem rather than coercive leverage. Industry and DOE reporting describe lead times of two years or more since 2022. Spare inventories are not publicly established.
components.source: NEIS assessment for this tool; not placed in the paper

components.label: Cables and conductors
components.description: Power cables and conductors.
components.notes: Ordinary electrical fittings where alternatives are plentiful (paper Appendix A4). The cable basket is attributed to several technologies and includes wooden poles (HS 44).
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4

components.label: Rare-earth separation and metal-making
components.description: Separating mixed rare-earth concentrate into individual oxides and reducing them to metal: the step before magnet-making.
components.criticalFunction: Magnet supply for defence systems and electric motors
components.notes: No substitute exists for the elements themselves in high-performance magnets. Refining shares are IEA figures for magnet rare earths (Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb). Stockpile cover is not publicly established.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1 and Appendix A4; IEA Critical Minerals Dataset 2026

components.label: Sintered NdFeB permanent magnets
components.description: High-performance magnets used in wind generators, EV motors and defence systems.
components.notes: China's April 2025 export licensing of heavy rare earths and magnets disrupted some automotive production within weeks (public reporting, May-June 2025). Ferrite magnets and induction motors substitute only at a performance cost. Coercion is judged on refining, the narrowest step; magnet trade itself is shown as secondary evidence.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1 and Appendix A4; IEA Critical Minerals Dataset 2026

components.label: Electric drive units and motors
components.description: Traction motors and integrated drive units for electric vehicles.
components.notes: Drive units integrate magnets and power electronics; the magnet dependency is assessed separately (ree-magnets).
components.source: NEIS assessment for this tool; not placed in the paper

components.label: Conventional crystalline-silicon modules
components.description: Mature, passive, globally traded solar modules.
components.notes: Solar is the paper's hard case (section 3): a large-yard good by default, with arguments for a limited domestic floor. Forced-labour restrictions apply regardless of yard. Next-generation PV is assessed separately.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 3 and Appendix A4

components.label: Solar cells and wafers
components.description: The cell and wafer steps upstream of module assembly.
components.notes: Whether cell and wafer production carries learning that matters for next-generation PV is contested; the learning questions are left Unknown rather than guessed.
components.source: NEIS assessment for this tool

components.label: Next-generation PV (perovskite and tandem cells)
components.description: Emerging cell architectures that could change the cost and performance basis of solar.
components.notes: The paper suggests next-generation PV may warrant medium-yard support. Leap-ahead tests (advantage, path to scale, evidence beyond novelty) are left to the reader.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 3

components.label: Passive racking and mounting
components.description: Steel and aluminium structures that hold modules. Tracker controllers are digitally active and should be assessed separately.
components.notes: Passive solar racking and mounting is a large-yard candidate in the paper.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 3 and Appendix A4

components.label: Reactor control and safety instrumentation
components.description: Digital instrumentation and control systems for reactor operation and protection.
components.notes: Safety systems are typically isolated from external networks under existing cyber-security rules, hence 'limited' external control.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), Appendix A4

components.label: HALEU enrichment
components.description: High-assay low-enriched uranium (5-20% U-235), needed by many advanced reactor designs.
components.criticalFunction: Fuel for advanced and research reactors
components.notes: Assessment, not data: Russia is currently the only commercial-scale HALEU supplier, and DOE describes commercial HALEU availability as limited. Trade codes (HS 2844.20) do not separate HALEU from LEU, so the trade evidence describes the broader fuel cycle. 'High' consequence for the advanced-reactor programme is contestable.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1; US DOE, HALEU Enrichment Services; US DOE (Jan 5 2026) enrichment awards

components.label: LEU enrichment services
components.description: Low-enriched uranium enrichment for today's light-water reactor fleet.
components.criticalFunction: Fuel for the operating reactor fleet
components.notes: The paper groups enrichment in the small yard. On this tool's tests, LEU turns on whether the largest non-coalition supplier exceeds the coercion line: Russia's export share is below it, and coalition enrichers (Urenco, Orano) are already qualified. Russia's share of world enrichment capacity is higher than its export share; test that in the scenario lab.
components.source: NEIS paper (Oct 2026), section 1; US DOE (Jan 5 2026) enrichment awards

stacks.label: Utility-scale battery storage
stacks.description: Control software, cells, materials, power electronics and balance of system, each judged on its own.

stacks.label: Grid-connected inverters and grid control
stacks.description: Where the security risk in grid equipment sits, and where it does not.

stacks.label: Rare-earth permanent magnets
stacks.description: From separated rare earths to the motors and generators that use them.

stacks.label: Solar PV
stacks.description: Solar is the paper's hard case: reasonable people can disagree, layer by layer.

stacks.label: Nuclear fuel and controls
stacks.description: Reactor controls, HALEU and LEU enrichment face different tests.
